 • Dems seize the House: Democrats will capture the House of Representatives , CNN’s Decision Desk projects, breaking the Republican stranglehold on Washington and setting up two years of confrontation with President Donald Trump.
 • Watching the Senate : Democrats are projected to flip at least two Senate seats, including in South Carolina where Annie Andrews will defeat Sen. Darline Graham. Democrats are also leading in other battleground Senate races. 
 • Historic election: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the first Black female governor in US history, CNN’s Decision Desk projects. In Florida, Republican Rep. Byron Donalds will be Florida’s next governor and make history as the first Black leader to hold the office.
 • Stay with us: See all the latest House and Senate results here . You can also sign up for CNN’s breaking news alerts .

 Republican Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders will win reelection in Arkansas, CNN projects
 By Jordan Budney 
 Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, on February 1. 
 Nathan Howard/Reuters 
 Republican Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders will win reelection in Arkansas, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, continuing the GOP hold on the seat in the red state.
 Sanders, who was White House press secretary during President Donald Trump’s first term, made history in 2022 as the first woman elected governor in Arkansas.
 She is the daughter of former Arkansas governor and current US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee.

 Jackson huddling with family and friends at election HQ as results pour in
 By Arlette Saenz in Portland, Maine
 Maine Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson is at the Holiday Inn in South Portland, Maine where his election night event is being held.
 While supporters are mingling in the public event space, Jackson is watching the results with his family and friends in a private area, said a campaign source, who added the team is feeling cautiously optimistic as results pour in.
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 Democrats secure the House after contentious race. Catch up on the latest
 By Taylor Romine 
 Watch party attendees react to election results confirming the US House of Representatives will flip from Republican to Democrat-controlled, at the AC Hotel Washington DC Capitol Hill Navy Yard on Tuesday. 
 Tom Brenner/Getty Images 
 After a long battle between Republicans and Democrats, CNN projects that Democrats will take the House — a monumental win that will shape the second half of President Donald Trump’s second term.
 It remains to be seen which party will control the Senate, but Democrats have had several important wins so far, including Democratic flips in North and South Carolina.
 Here is more of what’s happened in the last hour as results pour in:
 Fewer hurdles for a potential Ossoff presidential run: Among several big Democratic wins in Georgia so far, Keisha Lance Bottoms’ securing the governorship could enable a 2028 presidential run for Sen. Jon Ossoff who also won reelection. Ossoff has previously said he has “zero interest” in the office, but a Democrat holding Georgia’s top office would make it easier to replace the Senate seat and keep it filled within the party.
 Virginia protects abortion access through amendment: Virginia voters have added an amendment that will protect abortion access in the state. Nevada and Idaho also have similar amendments on their ballot, although those measures haven’t been called by CNN yet.
 FBI visits Alaska man who told reporter he may have voted wrong: As the Justice Department investigates the candidacy of a second Dan Sullivan, one Alaskan voter was visited by an FBI agent after telling a reporter he was concerned he voted for the wrong Sullivan. After reviewing a sample ballot, the man said he feels confident he voted for the Republican incumbent.
 White House defends Trump’s efforts: While some of Trump’s handpicked candidates are struggling , the White House is defending the president, saying he “did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves.”
 New York results are coming in: Several races in New York City were also called, with winners including House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries , who may on track to become the first Black speaker of the House.

 Top Democrat on oversight panel says "lawyer up" after Democrats projected to flip House
 By Annie Grayer 
 Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, said “lawyer up” in response to projections that the House will flip to Democratic control.
 Garcia is expected to launch a number of investigations into President Donald Trump, his family, and the administration’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

 Several progressive Democrats, including DSA members, will enter House in January
 By August Phillips 
 New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani raises his hands with Claire Valdez, Brad Lander and Darializa Avila Chevalier, who would all go on to win their elections in November, during a Get Out the Vote rally at in New York on June 18. 
 Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images 
 A number of progressives, including at least five members of the Democratic Socialists of America, will join the ranks of House Democrats in January after winning their elections tonight.
 Three of those progressives won in New York, where democratic socialists Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez , as well as former New York City comptroller Brad Lander , cruised to victory in deep-blue districts.
 DSA members also won in Colorado with Melat Kiros , Michigan with Donavan McKinney and Pennsylvania with Chris Rabb. Adam Hamawy , a progressive and sharp critic of Israel, won in New Jersey.
 While those candidates were all expected to win their general elections, the flurry of progressives who won their primaries and are now heading to the House this election cycle reflects the rising influence of the left wing of the Democratic Party as it takes control of the House majority .

 Democrat Bob Brooks will defeat GOP Rep. Ryan Mackenzie in PA’s 7th District, CNN projects
 By Logan Schiciano 
 Bob Brooks speaks an event in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on May 11. 
 Matt Rourke/AP 
 Democrat Bob Brooks will defeat Republican Rep. Ryan Mackenzie in Pennsylvania’s 7th District, CNN’s Decision Desk projects.
 Brooks’ victory puts the key seat in the state’s Lehigh Valley back in Democrats’ control after Mackenzie flipped it in 2024.
 The union president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association was a top recruit of Gov. Josh Shapiro’s as Democrats looked to oust four GOP incumbents in the state. On the campaign trail, Brooks emphasized his working-class roots, vowing to fight government corruption and address affordability.

 Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez will win Texas' 34th District, CNN projects
 By Aditi Sangal 
 Rep. Vicente González leaves the US Capitol on December 14, 2023. 
 Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc/Getty Images 
 Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez will win in Texas’ 34th Congressional District, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, preventing Republicans from picking up a House seat they targeted in redistricting efforts.
 The 34th is one of five Democratic-held districts that Texas Republicans targeted while redrawing maps last year, hoping to convert it into solidly red turf and add to House Speaker Mike Johnson’s slim GOP majority. However, the Hispanic-majority district turned out to be more competitive than initially expected as President Donald Trump’s standing with Latinos, who helped deliver him a second term, fell.

 Hakeem Jeffries on path to become first Black speaker of the House
 By Lauren Fox 
 House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks during a press conference with House Democrats in front of the steps to the US House of Representatives on December 18, 2025. 
 Samuel Corum/Sipa USA/AP 
 Democrats will flip the House, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, putting Rep. Hakeem Jeffries on a path to become the first Black speaker in history.
 The 56-year-old New Yorker won’t officially take that position until January 3, and he’ll need to spend the next several weeks shoring up votes among newly elected progressives and moderates alike.
 But inside the party, there is little doubt who will lead a newly resurgent Democratic party into the national spotlight for President Donald Trump’s final two years in the White House.
 Jeffries, who was just elected to his eighth term, rose quickly within the Democratic ranks, with key supporters within House leadership and within the powerful Congressional Black Caucus.
 The New Yorker has spoken often about the historical significance of his district in the civil rights movement; some of the neighborhoods he currently represents had been previously represented by Shirley Chisholm, who was the first Black woman elected to serve in Congress.
 “I stand on the shoulders of people like Shirley Chisolm and so many others as we work to advance the ball for everyday Americans,” Jeffries said when he became leader in 2022, making history then as the first Black American to lead a major political party in either chamber of Congress. He noted that the vote took place on what would have been Chisholm’s 98th birthday.
 Read more

 Democrats will win control of the House, CNN projects
 By Clare Foran 
 The US Capitol Dome in Washington, DC, in October 2026. 
 Ellie Merritt for CNN 
 Democrats will win control of the House, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, a major victory for the party that will now have power to pursue a sweeping oversight agenda targeting the Trump administration.
 The outcome of the election puts Hakeem Jeffries on a path to make history as the first Black speaker, though he will first have to win the gavel in a floor vote once the new Congress convenes.

 Democrat Annie Andrews will unseat GOP Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina, CNN projects
 By Dianne Gallagher 
 Annie Andrews speaks during a town hall campaign event in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, on October 21. 
 Win McNamee/Getty Images 
 Democrat Annie Andrews will win the US Senate race in South Carolina, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, defeating Sen. Darline Graham and flipping a seat that Republicans have held for nearly three decades.
 Andrews, a pediatrician, will become the first woman elected to the US Senate from South Carolina. The last time a Democrat won a Senate race in the Palmetto State was Fritz Hollings in 1998.
 It’s a stunning upset in a typically reliably Republican state that voted for President Donald Trump by nearly 18 percentage points in 2024, but also one that had been building since Graham became the GOP nominee in late August.
 Andrews, a 45-year-old mother of three, worked at Medical University of South Carolina for 15 years. She later started a nonprofit and political action committee and worked as a senior adviser to Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action.
 Andrews launched her Senate campaign last year acknowledging the uphill battle she faced running as a Democrat in South Carolina. She was originally running against GOP incumbent Sen. Lindsey Graham until he suddenly died in July.
 The governor appointed Darline Graham to finish her brother’s term, and she decided to run for the full term. With the help and backing of Trump, Graham eventually made it through a bruising special primary and runoff to become the GOP nominee. But the party didn’t immediately unite behind Graham and her campaign struggled, needing help from outside groups.

 It's 10 p.m. ET and polls are closing in Utah, Nevada and Montana
 By Ethan Cohen , Emilie Plesset and Elise Hammond 
 Clark County Election Department poll workers check people in to vote at the Meadows Mall in Las Vegas on Tuesday. 
 Ethan Miller/Getty Images 
 It’s 10 p.m. ET and final polls are now closing in Utah, Nevada and Montana.
 Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo is one of the most vulnerable Republican governors seeking reelection this cycle and his opponent, Democrat Attorney General Aaron Ford, is looking to flip the governor’s mansion with the support of Latino voters.
 Latinos are a critical voting group in Nevada. They made up 18% of the 2024 electorate, according to the CNN exit poll.
 In Montana’s 1st Congressional District, Sam Forstag, a first-time candidate and labor leader, is running an insurgent populist campaign against Army veteran Aaron Flint in a race that has forced Republicans to spend time and money defending the open seat.

 Judge issues emergency rules for ballot count after Westchester snafu
 By Gloria Pazmino 
 A New York State Supreme Court judge issued a consent order late Tuesday outlining conditions agreed to by the Republican and Democratic parties in Westchester County, hours after voting machine issues prevented hundreds of thousands of voters from scanning their ballots.
 The three-page consent order sets emergency rules for how unscanned ballots will be collected, secured and counted. Unscanned ballots are ones that weren’t run through the polling-site scanners. The final count will determine whether GOP Rep. Mike Lawler will be able to hold on to his seat against Democrat Cait Conley.
 Both parties jointly asked the court for a police-guarded, bipartisan-supervised process to move Westchester’s unscanned ballots to one central site in the county and count them there, starting no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday.
 The order also says both parties agreed to have county police escorts collect “all containers containing unscanned ballots” from every polling place in the county.
 The order says police must guard the ballots during transport and storage until the county canvass is completed. Once collected, the ballots will go into another sealed container, and the seal can be broken only in the presence of representatives of both parties, the order says.

 Democratic socialist Janeese Lewis George will win mayoral race in DC, CNN projects
 By Morgan Leason 
 Janeese Lewis George gives an interview with members of the news media during Washington, DC’s primary voting day, June 16. 
 Leah Millis/Reuters 
 City Councilwoman Janeese Lewis George will win the mayoral race in Washington, DC, CNN’s Decision Desk projects.
 Lewis George, a democratic socialist, will face unique challenges in her interactions with the federal government, as President Donald Trump threatened to “take back Washington” if she were elected.
 The politician has been critical of outgoing Democratic Mayor Muriel Bowser, who often took the middle ground between working with the administration and asserting DC’s rights following the Trump administration’s takeover of Washington’s Metropolitan Police Department last summer and ongoing deployment of National Guard troops to the city.
 Now Lewis George will have to stake out her own direction in DC, where Trump will remain the city’s most famous resident for another two years.

 Link Copied!
 Mood at Andrews campaign HQ in SC has shifted from watch party to real party
 By Dianne Gallagher 
 Supporters of South Carolina Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews cheer during her election night watch party, in Charleston, South Carolina, on Tuesday. 
 Mic Smith/AP 
 The mood at Annie Andrews HQ in Charleston, South Carolina, has been upbeat all night, but in the past few minutes it’s shifted from watch party to real party.
 People have started to gather on stage, dancing as the crowd of supporters sings along to the Natasha Bedingfield song “Unwritten.”
 Democrats close to the campaign still say they are cautiously optimistic, but they’re saying it with smiles on their faces at this point as returns continue to trend positively for Andrews in a state President Donald Trump won just two years ago by nearly 18 points
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 “Georgia, you did it”: Ossoff celebrates critical Senate win
 By Elise Hammond 
 Sen. Jon Ossoff reacts during an election night rally in Atlanta on Tuesday. 
 Carlos Barria/Reuters 
 Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff thanked voters in Georgia for reelecting him in a state that voted for President Donald Trump two years ago.
 “Georgia, you did it,” Ossoff said.
 He is the first Democratic senator elected to a second full term in Georgia since 1990, defending a critical Democrat-held seat.
 Ossoff painted his win as a rebuke of what he called “the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the failed lame duck president, Donald J. Trump.”
 He said this is a moment “not for restoration, but for reformation” as he laid out the work that is yet to be done to address American’s concerns about things like affordability and healthcare.

 Nervous energy at Hinson campaign watch party
 By Steve Contorno in Cedar Rapids, Iowa
 The energy at the Cedar Rapids election results watch party for Rep. Ashley Hinson is decidedly subdued as they await results in her Iowa Senate race.
 Some people are sitting in chairs watching Fox News’ somber broadcast projecting Republican losses elsewhere on two large screens. Chitchatting is getting drowned out by Sean Hannity and Trey Gowdy trying to diagnose the GOP’s woes. The hotel bar isn’t getting many customers and the room is only about 70% full, 45 minutes after polls closed.
 Tepid applause broke out when Fox announced Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders won reelection.
 Hinson’s team remains optimistic by the day’s high turnout, particularly in rural parts of the state, and by signs of ticket-splitting in other contests, like South Carolina, which they see as key to their chances. But expectations that Hinson could help save a GOP majority are increasingly giving way to hope that she will be one of the lone bright spots for Republicans in the face of what is shaping up to be a good night for Democrats.
 CNN’s Joel Williams contributed to this report.

 Knives starting to come out against House GOP leadership
 By Annie Grayer in Shreveport, Louisiana
 With Democrats flipping a district in Kentucky, a district that Trump won by 15 points, some Republicans are starting to point the blame at all House Republican leadership. The Kentucky 6th Congressional District race was one that House Speaker Mike Johnson and his team said they’d be watching closely, as CNN previously reported.
 “Many republicans are wondering how ANYONE in House Leadership will survive these results,” a GOP operative told CNN.
 But other Republicans say the blame should fall more squarely on President Donald Trump, whose low approval rating and decision to go to war with Iran made it a difficult environment for Republicans.
 One GOP lawmaker told CNN “Trump first and foremost” is getting the most heat in the blame game already playing out behind the scenes.

 Democrat Rebecca Bennett will oust GOP Rep. Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey, CNN projects
 By Ellis Kim 
 New Jersey Democratic Congressional candidate Rebecca Bennett arrives to a rally at Raritan Valley Community College in Branchburg, New Jersey, on October 16. 
 Kena Betancur/Getty Images 
 Democrat Rebecca Bennett will win the election for New Jersey’s 7th District, CNN’s Decision Desk projects, flipping a seat held by Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr. after his lengthy absence from Washington.
 The Democratic Party had long targeted this affluent suburban district, and its efforts were probably helped this cycle after Kean was mysteriously absent from Congress for nearly four months in the spring.
 The congressman revealed in his late June return that he had been receiving treatment for depression. While President Donald Trump and GOP leaders stuck by Kean, supporting his reelection bid, the episode became a saga that drew national attention.
 Bennett, a former Navy helicopter pilot, returns the swing seat to Democratic control after Kean defeated former Rep. Tom Malinowski in 2022 and flipped the seat red.
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 Trump officials already blaming losses on those who pushed Iran war
 By Kristen Holmes 
 Administration officials and President Donald Trump’s allies are already pinning blame for tonight’s results on those they say encouraged him to go to war with Iran.
 Trump’s top political advisers had privately warned for months that the war would likely lead to Republican shortfalls this cycle, and Trump has privately vented that it badly damaged his party’s midterm chances, sources familiar with the matter told CNN.
 As of just before 10 p.m., Trump was still in the East Room watching results, a White House official said.
 Some Trump allies expect he will find someone to take the blame for GOP losses. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has been a proponent of the war, is seen by some allies as potentially vulnerable. Trump, always one to crowdsource an opinion, has asked allies about their thoughts on Hegseth’s performance of late.
 “The bottom line is that Trump feels misled — he was misled,” one Trump adviser told CNN. “And somebody should pay for that.”
 However, Trump has continued to defend Hegseth publicly and dismissed congressional efforts to remove him, calling him “great warrior.”
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 White House starts to blame Trump's handpicked candidates
 By Kaitlan Collins 
 Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley speaks as President Donald Trump looks on during a campaign rally in Gastonia, North Carolina, on September 16. 
 Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images 
 As President Donald Trump’s handpicked candidates are struggling in the midterms Tuesday night, a White House official is offering this assessment: “President Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves.”
 The candidates might argue the opposite, as Ken Paxton in Texas and Darline Graham in South Carolina are potentially in trouble, and Michael Whatley has conceded his race in North Carolina.
 Despite that, the official insisted the White House mood is defiant, arguing Trump is the real draw for GOP voters.
 “President Trump was not on the ballot, and it’s proven that Trump voters show up when he is on the ballot,” the official said.
 Among the other White House claims:
 “Anyone who voted Democrat today is going to have a serious case of buyers remorse when gas prices come down quickly when the Iran conflict is solved but they’re still stuck with a list of liberal extremist Democrats.”
 “And a final note here: regardless of how today plays out, President Trump’s resolve to stop the Radical Left is only going to become stronger.”
 “Buckle up,” the White House official said.
